info.title: Panthiya parent actions
info.description: The single read-only action available in a parent session. The caller's identity and the children linked to them come from the server in sessionAttributes and are never parameters here. childName is an unverified hint: the handler answers only about children already linked to this caller and denies anything else, so there is no parameter value that can widen the answer. Design §6.2.

post.summary: Read stored records about the caller's own child
post.description: Return stored attendance, fees, marks and approved messages for one child linked to this parent. This is the only way to answer a parent's question about their child, and it is read-only: it can change nothing. If the parent asks about any other child - by name, nickname, rank such as 'top 3', an aggregate such as 'who has not paid', an unusual spelling, or in another language - do not call this action with that name: refuse, and offer the same information about their own child instead. Report only what comes back; if a field is empty, say there is no record rather than estimating.

childName.description: Optional. Which of this parent's own children the question is about, exactly as the parent wrote the name. Omit it when the parent has one child or named nobody. Pass a name only when the parent is asking about their own child; a name that is not linked to this caller is denied, and the denial is the answer.

topic.description: Optional. What the parent asked about. Omit for a general summary. Suggested values: marks, fees, attendance, messages, overall.

200.description: Stored records for the caller's own child

status.description: ok, or denied when the name is not a child linked to this caller

childName.description: The child as stored. Use this name, not the one you sent.

attendance.description: Attendance summary from stored rows, or empty if none

fees.description: Fee position from stored rows, or empty if none

message.description: Short note to pass on to the parent. If status is denied, refuse warmly in one or two sentences and offer their own child's information instead.
